references.text: Contains the detailed laws about leprosy that priests were to teach the people, as referred to in Deuteronomy 24:8.
Describes the cleansing rituals for leprosy that Levitical priests were to perform and teach.
The story of Miriam being struck with leprosy, an example of how leprosy was handled in Israel.
The story of Na'aman being healed of leprosy, showing the priests' role in declaring purity.
King Uzziah was struck with leprosy as punishment and had to live in isolation, in accordance with the laws about leprosy.
Jesus heals a leper and sends him to the priest to show himself, in accordance with the Law of Moses.
Jesus heals ten lepers and sends them to the priests to be declared clean, as the law prescribed.
